top_story: Israel’s admission on 20 August that its soldiers fired on the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab and six relatives were killed, followed by a formal investigation announced by 22 August, sharpens scrutiny of a wartime accountability system that Palestinians view as too narrow and too late. Hind’s mother’s demand for justice beyond an internal probe reflects a wider collapse of trust in Israeli institutions, especially as Gaza’s civilian trauma remains inseparable from the silencing of those documenting it after the killing of more than 250 media workers. That climate is reinforced by Itamar Ben-Gvir’s public advocacy for executing Palestinians convicted in military courts while excluding Jewish extremists, signaling an increasingly explicit unequal legal order rather than a fringe provocation. The combined effect is to deepen Palestinian expectations of impunity, harden international concern over Israeli conduct, and further erode any political space for de-escalation.
